FireScope: Satellite-Based Wildfire Monitoring and Early Warning System

FireScope is a satellite-powered wildfire monitoring and decision-support platform that uses NASA's MODIS and VIIRS active-fire datasets, accessed through NASA FIRMS. It processes near-real-time satellite observations to identify potential fire hotspots, visualize their geographical locations, and assess detection attributes such as confidence and Fire Radiative Power (FRP).

The platform aims to combine satellite observations with environmental data, including weather conditions, rainfall, vegetation and terrain, to provide better context for identifying areas of potential fire risk. Through interactive mapping, historical analysis and hotspot monitoring, FireScope seeks to make wildfire information more accessible and useful for timely decision-making.

The project addresses the challenge of monitoring fires across large and remote areas where ground-based observation may be limited. By leveraging freely accessible NASA Earth observation data, FireScope aims to support environmental monitoring, improve situational awareness and assist communities and emergency responders in making informed decisions.
details:
FireScope: Satellite-Based Wildfire Monitoring and Decision-Support System

FireScope is a wildfire monitoring platform designed to improve the detection, visualization and understanding of potential fire activity using NASA Earth observation data.

How it works

The platform retrieves active-fire observations from NASA's Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS), primarily using MODIS and VIIRS satellite datasets. VIIRS provides approximately 375-metre spatial resolution, enabling more detailed hotspot monitoring. The system processes geographical coordinates, acquisition timestamps, detection confidence and Fire Radiative Power (FRP) to identify and visualize potential fire activity on an interactive map.

We also explore integrating environmental information such as temperature, rainfall, wind conditions, vegetation and terrain to provide additional context for assessing fire risk. Historical observations can help identify recurring fire activity and monitor changes over time.

Benefits and intended impact

FireScope aims to make satellite-derived fire information easier to understand and access. It can help environmental researchers, forest monitoring authorities and emergency response teams identify areas requiring attention, improve situational awareness and support informed decisions. Its intended impact is to contribute towards more effective wildfire monitoring and environmental protection, particularly in remote areas.

Tools and technologies

  • Data sources: NASA FIRMS, MODIS and VIIRS.
  • Programming: Python for data acquisition and processing.
  • Libraries: Pandas and Requests for data handling and API integration.
  • Visualization: Interactive geographical mapping.
  • Environmental data: NASA Earth observation and weather datasets.

Creativity and innovation

The creative aspect of FireScope lies in combining multiple freely accessible satellite datasets into a unified monitoring platform. Rather than displaying isolated fire detections, it aims to provide geographical context, historical patterns and environmental information to make satellite observations more meaningful.

Factors considered

Our team considered satellite resolution, data availability, observation delays, detection confidence, false positives, cloud interference, geographical coverage and accessibility. We also recognized that a satellite hotspot does not always indicate a wildfire and that intermittent satellite observations cannot guarantee continuous monitoring. These limitations are important when designing a reliable decision-support system.
